findings.problem: PacketWorkflow uses raw booleans and strings instead of a typestate enum to enforce valid lifecycle transitions. Callers can construct states where is_validated=false and status="sent", or where is_sent=true but sent_at_epoch_ms is None.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid protocol states are representable; a packet can be marked sent without being validated, or sent without a timestamp, violating domain invariants silently.
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms with a single PacketState enum with explicit variants (e.g., Unvalidated, Validated, Sent { sent_at: u64 }) that make illegal states unrepresentable at the type level.

findings.problem: status is a public String field. The mark_sent function sets it to a magic string literal "sent". Any caller can set status to any value, including invalid or contradictory states.
findings.failure_mode: Status values are unchecked literals, enabling states like status="invalid" while is_sent=true, or status="sent" on a freshly constructed PacketWorkflow without any lifecycle discipline.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with `pub status: PacketStatus` where PacketStatus is a sealed enum with only valid domain values (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent, Failed). Use smart constructors or enum variants for construction.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are separate lifecycle booleans that can be in inconsistent combinations (e.g., is_sent=true, is_validated=false, status="pending").
findings.failure_mode: Booleans encode an unstructured state space (2^3 = 8 combinations for status+is_validated+is_sent) with no enforcement of valid transitions; callers can arbitrarily flip booleans or construct them with contradictory values.
findings.fix: Replace all three fields (status, is_validated, is_sent) with a single typestate enum that encodes the lifecycle. Each variant carries only the data it needs (e.g., Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }).

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is an Option<u64> living outside the typestate machine. It can be None while is_sent=true, or Some while is_sent=false, with no correlation enforced by types.
findings.failure_mode: A packet can be marked sent (is_sent=true) with no timestamp (sent_at_epoch_ms=None), or have a timestamp with no sent flag, because the Option is decoupled from the lifecycle state.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the typestate enum variant that owns it. E.g., PacketState::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } — the u64 is mandatory in the Sent variant, making None impossible when sent.

findings.problem: id is a public String raw primitive. No validation, uniqueness, or format enforcement exists. Any caller can set id to an empty string, null bytes, or an invalid format.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid or empty IDs are representable; downstream systems may break on empty strings or malicious input. The id carries domain rules that are not enforced by the type system.
findings.fix: Replace `pub id: String` with a newtype `PacketId(String)` or `PacketId([u8; N])` with a fallible smart constructor that validates format (e.g., non-empty, valid encoding). Make the field private.

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String, bool, u64, Option) cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors. PacketWorkflow accepts unvalidated external input directly, and callers can construct invalid domain states without any parsing or validation layer.
findings.failure_mode: Hostile or malformed external input (empty strings, invalid epoch values, contradictory booleans) reaches core logic without transformation into trusted domain types, enabling invalid packet states throughout the system.
findings.fix: Introduce fallible smart constructors (e.g., PacketWorkflow::parse_from_raw fields -> Result<Self, ParseError>) at module boundaries. Core logic consumes only validated domain types. Parse strings into newtypes, convert booleans into typestate enum transitions, and reject invalid combinations.

findings.problem: All fields of PacketWorkflow are pub, allowing callers to mutate any field directly without going through typed transitions. mark_sent only sets fields but callers can bypass it entirely.
findings.failure_mode: Direct field mutation bypasses any invariants, enabling states that mark_sent cannot produce or prevent.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide only typed constructors and transition methods (e.g., PacketWorkflow::validate(), PacketWorkflow::mark_sent()) that enforce valid state transitions.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses a magic string literal "sent" for status. This is brittle, unsearchable, and easy to misspell across the codebase.
findings.failure_mode: Typos in status strings (e.g., "snt", "SENT") produce silent logic errors rather than compile-time failures.
findings.fix: Replace the string literal with an enum variant or const from a typed PacketStatus enum.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for mark_sent or any performance claim. The function does a .to_string() allocation on every call.
findings.failure_mode: Performance characteristics of mark_sent (heap allocation for status string) are unmeasured and unbounded; in a hot path this could cause allocation pressure.
findings.fix: Add benchmarks measuring mark_sent allocation cost and latency. If called frequently, replace String with a &'static str from an enum or use an interned/inline-string representation.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent allocation and latency
no profiler evidence showing hot path behavior of PacketWorkflow transitions
no allocation audit for .to_string() on every mark_sent call
no second-ring evidence (compiler artifacts, IR, or assembly) for the stated design
residual_risk: Static review only. No commands were run. The crate has fundamental type-level defects: all lifecycle state is represented by raw primitives (String, bool, Option) that make illegal states representable, public fields allow arbitrary mutation, and mark_sent uses a magic string literal instead of a typed enum. A developer can construct a PacketWorkflow in any of 8+ contradictory states without any type-system enforcement. The fix requires replacing the entire struct fields with a single typestate enum, newtypes for domain IDs, and fallible parse-boundary constructors.
